not_testable.T1055.012: Process hollowing is visible only through memory and API-call telemetry (suspended create, unmap, write, resume); Kavach collects process command lines, so a synthetic command line cannot demonstrate the behavior.
not_testable.T1055.009: Proc-memory injection needs write-to-another-process memory telemetry that Kavach does not collect.
not_testable.T1055: Generic process injection needs API-level or memory telemetry that Kavach does not collect.
not_testable.T1055.001: DLL injection needs remote-thread and image-load API telemetry; only module-load events and command lines are collected.
not_testable.T1014: A rootkit hides itself from the very process and file listings the sensor reads; synthetic events cannot represent absence.
not_testable.T1205.002: Socket filter backdoors need kernel packet-filter telemetry that Kavach does not collect.
not_testable.T1565.001: Stored data manipulation needs content-integrity telemetry (before/after content), not file metadata.
not_testable.T1027.002: Software packing needs static binary analysis of file content; Kavach events carry no file bytes.
not_testable.T1573.002: Encrypted channel detection needs TLS or flow-content telemetry that Kavach does not collect.
not_testable.T1030: Transfer size limits need per-flow byte-volume telemetry; network events carry only a destination.
not_testable.T1550.003: Pass-the-ticket needs Kerberos ticket telemetry beyond the auth event fields Kavach models.
not_testable.T1110.002: Password cracking happens offline on attacker infrastructure; no process, file, network or auth event is generated on the victim.
not_testable.T1078.003: A successful login with a valid local account is indistinguishable from legitimate use without a per-user baseline or identity-provider context; auth events carry only user, source and outcome.
not_testable.T1078.004: Valid cloud account use is visible only in cloud control-plane (IdP / CloudTrail) logs; Kavach collects endpoint process, file, network, registry, auth and module events, and a CLI call proves nothing about credential legitimacy.
not_testable.T1204.001: Whether a user followed a malicious link is a human action; a browser opening a URL is identical to normal browsing and needs URL reputation and email context Kavach does not collect.
not_testable.T1068: Exploitation of a kernel or SUID bug is visible only through crash, memory or syscall telemetry; a command line cannot demonstrate it (a named exploit binary would only test name matching).
not_testable.T1554: Detecting a modified host binary needs file-content integrity (hash before and after) and file events carry no content; a path write is only a weak proxy.
not_testable.T1221: Template injection happens inside the document XML: Office fetches the remote template itself, the process command line holds only a local path, and network events carry a destination but no owning process, so the behavior cannot be shown from the telemetry Kavach collects (a first scenario using a network-only sequence missed, see docs).
